stops.note: a thrown disc; Myron's bronze Discobolus (c. 450 BC) shows an athlete about to throw one
a quoit, then a round platter; the same word later gave English desk, dais, disc and disk
borrowed into Old English as disc 'plate'; the 'satellite dish' followed the first satellite TV links of the 1960s

current_meaning: a shallow container for cooking or serving food; a particular food
